item.title: Navy sailor on USS Lincoln says dad was arrested by immigration officials
item.description: Historically rare, immigration arrests of military spouses and parents have become more common under the second Trump administration.

item.title: USS Lincoln sailor's dad arrested by ICE, family says
item.description: U.S. Navy sailor Joshua Aviles, who is aboard the USS Abraham Lincoln, says he learned his father was arrested by federal immigration officials. Camilo Montoya-Galvez reports.

item.title: Trump administration's ICE detains Navy sailor's dad, sends Latino migrants to Africa
item.description: A Navy sailor deployed aboard the USS Abraham Lincoln says ICE detained his dad while he is overseas. This comes as more details are emerging about migrants being deported to countries in Africa. CBS News' Camilo Montoya-Galvez.

item.title: Jared Kushner and Hakeem Jeffries met as midterm elections loom
item.description: The meeting came with Democrats expected to take control of the House in the November elections, which would put Jeffries in line to become the next House speaker.

item.title: Principal sacrifices job to help homeless student
item.description: A former Ohio principal lost his job after allowing a homeless student to remain in school after the district unenrolled him. He and his wife eventually became the student's legal guardians. CBS News contributor David Begnaud shares the story.

item.title: Trump announces 50% tariffs on Canadian automotive and steel imports
item.description: President Trump said tariffs on Canadian automotive and steel imports will rise to 50% on January 1, 2027, in a social media post.

item.title: How Trump's economic offensives against Iran and Canada will impact American wallets
item.description: President Trump is imposing tariffs on Canada after talks stalled. This comes as the White House prepares to announce more sanctions against Iran. Threadneedle's Ann Berry joins CBS News with her take, and Shikha Jain, a partner at Simon-Kucher, joins with more insight.

item.title: Here's how much interest a $40,000 5-year CD account can earn savers now
item.description: Opening a $40,000 5-year CD account now could be a smart choice for savers. Here's how much interest they'd earn.

item.title: Levi Zhang of "Cooking with Levi" shares advice for kids who want to be better cooks
item.description: Levi Zhang and his parents share some recipes from their new cookbook and talk about how their viral videos started.

item.title: Watch Live: Lindsay Clancy trial continues with psychiatrist on stand
item.description: The Lindsay Clancy trial​ resumed with a psychiatrist back on the stand as testimony winds down in the Massachusetts murder case.

item.title: Trump targets Canada and Iran with economic pressure
item.description: The Trump administration is navigating rough waters with Canada and Iran by applying economic pressure. CBS News' Aaron Navarro and Aaron MacLean have more.

item.title: U.S. set to unveil "economic D-Day" sanctions against Iran
item.description: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said new sanctions being imposed on Iran would amount to the "greatest financial offensive" ever.

item.title: Ted Cruz says Texas Senate race will be a "$200 million" fight
item.description: GOP Sen. Ted Cruz outlined the road ahead for Republicans as Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton faces off against state Rep. James Talarico in the closely watched contest.

item.title: How ADHD and Rejection Sensitive Dysphoria are linked
item.description: Dr. Sasha Hamdani, a board-certified psychiatrist and ADHD clinical specialist, joins "CBS Mornings" to discuss the relationship between ADHD and Rejection Sensitive Dysphoria, also known as RSD.

item.title: What happens if a debt collector garnishes more than you owe?
item.description: An excessive garnishment can cost you, but there may be ways to recover money that shouldn't have been taken.

item.title: Ted Cruz says he thinks Canada's tariff response is "a little performative"
item.description: GOP Sen. Ted Cruz joins "CBS Mornings" to discuss his new book, "Going Further: The Incomparable Clarence Thomas," and weigh in on the U.S.-Canada trade feud and the Senate race in Texas between Ken Paxton and James Talarico.

item.title: Chinese humanoid robot beats Usain Bolt's sprint world record
item.description: Two human records were smashed by robots competing in the Olympics-like World Humanoid Robot Games in China.

item.title: How long before China is ready to deploy humanoid robot soldiers?
item.description: A Chinese robotics developer tells CBS News humanoids won't turn against humans as they're just machines: "It all depends on who controls them."

item.description: Since then, more than 200 people have been killed in U.S. strikes in the eastern Pacific Ocean and Caribbean Sea.

item.title: Chinese robot beats Usain Bolt's running record
item.description: Robots are competing in China, showcasing new skills that may beat records set by humans. CBS News' Anna Coren reports from Beijing.

item.title: Ex-NBA center ejected from WNBA game after being confronted by player
item.description: The WNBA has been the subject of recent debates on whether transgender women should be allowed to participate in the league.

item.title: Young pilot makes emergency ocean landing in Florida near busy beach
item.description: A young pilot was forced to make an emergency landing in the ocean near a busy beach in Boca Raton, Florida. Tom Hanson reports.

item.title: Harry and Meghan's U.K. move sparks major speculation
item.description: Prince Harry and Meghan Markle's surprising announcement has fans speculating if Meghan Markle may be eyeing a return to acting. Roya Nikkhah reports.

item.title: Republican, Democratic strategists react to data centers becoming a huge voting issue
item.description: Republican and Democratic voters are slamming data centers being built in their communities as they prepare to take their concerns to the polls. Political strategists Harrison Fields and Sam Newton join with their take.

item.title: Lindsay Clancy murder trial closing arguments could begin
item.description: Closing arguments in the trial for Lindsay Clancy, the Massachusetts mom accused of killing her three children, could begin as soon as Monday as the prosecution continues calling rebuttal witnesses. Caroline Polisi has more.

item.title: 2 takes on Lindsay Clancy's state of mind at the time of the alleged crimes
item.description: Experts testifying at the Lindsay Clancy trial offered different takes on her state of mind at the time when she allegedly killed her three children. CBS News legal contributor Rebecca Roiphe breaks down the testimony.

item.title: Laptop catches fire on flight to Dallas
item.description: A laptop caught fire during an American Airlines flight from Atlanta to Dallas on Friday, ramping up concern over lithium batteries overheating. Kris Van Cleave has the latest.

item.title: Navy sailor has been on USS Lincoln for 9 months. He just found out ICE took his dad.
item.description: U.S. Navy sailor Joshua Aviles, who has been deployed aboard the USS Abraham Lincoln in the Middle East for nine months, says his father was detained by U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement. CBS News' Camilo Montoya-Galvez reports.

item.title: Trump administration to announce new sanctions on Iran after 50% tariffs on Canada
item.description: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent is set to announce a new set of sanctions against Iran. Meanwhile, Canada's Mark Carney reacted to the Trump administration's 50% tariff on Canadian goods, saying Canada would match the fees "dollar for dollar." Weijia Jiang has the latest.

item.title: Out-of-control Hawk Fire in Reno keeping tens of thousands evacuated
item.description: Shifting winds challenged firefighters battling the out-of-control Hawk Fire in Reno, Nevada, that was keeping tens of thousands of people evacuated.
